target_customer: Social web users who wanted their identity and content hosted on their own sites
problem: Online identity was locked inside individual social networks.

founders.name: Paul McKellar
founders.background_notes: YC page: later worked in social media, payments (Square/Block) and social publishing, now mostly an LP with angel investments.

founders.name: Philipp Pfeiffenberger
founders.background_notes: YC page: after Deluux led photosharing and mobile games at Slide, later anti-fraud and security work at Google.

technical_complexity.rationale: Distributing personalized content across independent sites needs identity and syndication plumbing, which was unsolved in 2008; the product never launched.

defensibility.rationale: No users and no launched product, and open web efforts were developing similar ideas in public.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Facebook Connect (July 2008) and Google Friend Connect gave sites social identity without a new network; Deluux never launched.

market_need_then: Demand was unproven: YC says it had yet to launch. Context was the open web push (OpenID, DiSo) against closed networks.

brand_strength.rationale: No sources on the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Deluux went through YC W08 with a two person team aiming to be a distributed Facebook, but never launched according to YC. Facebook Connect and Google Friend Connect arrived within months and no funding or press followed. The founders moved on to Slide, Square and Google roles per the YC page. The stated cause is not public, so factors are inferred and uncertain.
notes: Company site returned HTTP 503. Funding: Seedtable shows last funding 2008 with no amount, so the round is recorded with null amount and rests on a single database (Seedtable); the YC standard deal is the likely source but this is not stated. Competitor list empty: the YC text names Facebook and Ning but no source dated at the batch was opened. Failure factors are inferences. Exit unknown because no shutdown notice exists.
